SMTO-CFG-0026 — A Gateway chosen for this message is missing or turned off

GUID: abedf71c-02e1-455d-91b9-b822e11a546a
Slug: composer-gateway-unavailable
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The message box is set to use a Gateway (a computer SMTO runs commands on) that has been removed or switched off. SMTO didn't start the task.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select the button above the message box that starts with Target: (or shows Multiple gateways). Select Controls first if you don't see it. Remove any Gateway marked × and choose one marked ✓. A Gateway marked × is off or can't be used, while ✓ means it is on and connected.
  2. If the Gateway you need was switched off, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and turn its switch On. SMTO only sends work to Gateways that are turned on.
  3. Send your message again once the Target button shows the Gateway you want. The message is accepted once every Gateway it names exists and is turned on.

What success looks like

  • Your message starts a task, and the Target button shows the Gateway you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. If the Gateway was deleted, ask them to add it again with + Add Gateway in Settings › Setup › Gateways; don't keep resending until a Gateway is available.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Composer submission validation refused the request because a selected primary or additional Gateway ID is not in the Gateway registry or is disabled.

What this means

  • A selected primary/additional Gateway record is absent or disabled during composer submission validation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • A selected primary/additional Gateway record is absent or disabled during composer submission validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect every selected Gateway ID and enabled flag; this check alone is not a live network-health probe.

How to fix it

  • Every ID in composer_values.gateway_selection.gateway_ids (or gateway_id) must exist in the Gateway registry with enabled=true. Re-enable or re-register the Gateway in Settings › Setup › Gateways, or select an enabled one; connectivity is checked later by normal readiness and admission.
  • Select existing enabled Gateways for new work, then let their ordinary readiness checks establish availability.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • All intended selected Gateway records exist and are enabled before normal readiness/admission checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
